pr_title: Validate nfconntrack regardless of kernel version
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Ricardo Pchevuzinske Katz <ricardo.katz@gmail.com>

**What type of PR is this?**

/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**: Due to Red Hat 8.3+ using Kernel 4.18 but new nf_conntrack, kube-proxy does not try to load nf_conntrack correctly.

This PR removes the validation based in kernel version and validates the ability to use kube-proxy IPVS based in the existence of nf_conntrack or nf_conntrack_v4

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:  
Fixes #97052

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```

**Additional documentation e.g., KEPs (Kubernetes Enhancement Proposals), usage docs, etc.**:

/sig network
/priority backlog

/assign @danwinship @andrewsykim

so, I think we were checking based on kernel version  based in this patch https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/a0ae2562c6c4b2721d9fddba63b7286c13517d9f

> so, I think we were checking based on kernel version based in this patch [torvalds/linux@a0ae256](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/a0ae2562c6c4b2721d9fddba63b7286c13517d9f)

Yeap, this was commented in the Code. But apparently RH backported to Kernel v4.18 this approach, which triggers a warning for users using RH 8.3

Anyway, I think that removing the logics based in Kernel version and assuming we may have multiple nf_conntrack modules and at least one must be loaded seems a better approach :)

ip_vs depends on nf_conntrack since 2.6.37, so no need to try to load it I would say
https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/dba4490d22a496f9b7c21919cf3effbed5851213

I'm more likely to be excessive careful here then simple removing the need of nf_conntrack loading.

Also, there are some scenarios (like the one with fully statically compiled kernels) that's hard to detect if the module is there or not.

I understand that when compiling the kernel and selecting ip_vs the nf_conntrack might be selected automatically before the dependency of the symbols, but will leave this for the reviewers! 

Thanks for the follow up!!

issue_context.title: kube-proxy IPVS tries to load nf_conntrack_ipv4 on RedHat 8.3+
issue_context.body:
**What happened**:
kube-proxy IPVS tries to load nf_conntrack_ipv4 on RedHat 8.3+ (so soon on CentOS ;) )
RedHat 8.3 has kernel 4.18 with many backports, including nf_conntrack_ipv4 removed/merged into nf_conntrack
https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/8/html/8.3_release_notes/new-features#enhancement_networking

**What you expected to happen**:
kube-proxy (and kubernetes components in general) do not use kernel versions to influence behavior

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Run Kubernetes on RedHat 8.3+ or CentOS streams

**Anything else we need to know?**:
This is just a warning, not a blocker
```
# kubectl logs -n kube-system pod/kube-proxy-8w2tx
W1203 12:48:28.105739       1 proxier.go:635] Failed to load kernel module nf_conntrack_ipv4 with modprobe. You can ignore this message when kube-proxy is running inside container without mounting /lib/modules
W1203 12:48:28.132811       1 proxier.go:635] Failed to load kernel module nf_conntrack_ipv4 with modprobe. You can ignore this message when kube-proxy is running inside container without mounting /lib/modules
```

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.18.10
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: VMs
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.3 (Ootpa)
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 4.18.0-240.1.1.el8_3.x86_64
- Install tools: Kubespray
comments: /sig network

Hello @champtar 

Can you, anyway confirm that when the other modules are loaded?

Per the [code](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/38f5dc8e7b75c16db29105b7c2314bfd3100840d/pkg/util/ipvs/ipvs.go#L129) yes, it checks if the kernel is less then 4.19 and loads the "nf_conntrack_ipv4" so this needs to be reverified.

Yes the modules are loaded by kube-proxy
```
# lsmod | grep ip_vs
ip_vs_sh               16384  0
ip_vs_wrr              16384  0
ip_vs_rr               16384  6
ip_vs                 172032  12 ip_vs_rr,ip_vs_sh,ip_vs_wrr
nf_conntrack          172032  6 xt_conntrack,nf_nat,nft_ct,ipt_MASQUERADE,nf_conntrack_netlink,ip_vs
nf_defrag_ipv6         20480  2 nf_conntrack,ip_vs
libcrc32c              16384  4 nf_conntrack,nf_nat,xfs,ip_vs
```

this ticket is for
- the warning (at least now it's "documented")
- the good practice of not using kernel version to detect features (to be nice with CentOS / RHEL users :) )

Got it :)

I'll take a look into the module loader to see if trying to load one then other and raising the error if both fails is a better approach ;)
/triage accepted
I've looked at some systems (EL7, 8.2, 8.3), and ip_vs always depends on nf_conntrack

To be clear kube-proxy is working just fine, with a warning. kubespray needed some love (merged but not released)

review_comments:
You're hardcoding in two different places the fact that all of the modules returned by `GetRequiredIPVSModules` are required, _except_ for those two, which you only need one of... that's a confusing API.

If you want to be really abstract, `GetRequiredIPVSModules` could return a `[][]string`, where each element of the outer array is an array of equivalent modules, and the caller would make sure that at least one module from each element was present:
